title: Amber Lane shift log - midday escalation and runbook notes
notes:
Summary:
- Shift: Amber Lane (12:00-20:00 PT) handoff. Took over from Jackson at 12:05. Short window for context sync due to simultaneous incident.
- Primary focus: intermittent tokenization failures + downstream cache eviction storms causing tail latency spikes to 2.1s p95 on hosted-api-gen routes.
- Current state: degraded-but-serviceable. Autoscaler stabilized at +2 pools; error rate trending down but still ~0.6% above baseline on /v1/generate for 512+ token requests.

Timeline (high level):
- 12:10 — First spike detected by alert INF-P95-LAT-3x. Pager routed to oncall.
- 12:13 — Slack thread started: #sre-ops "tokenize-failures". Notified model-runtime team (Maria).
- 12:20 — Identified correlation between large-batch KV cache invalidations and GC churn on dedicated pools.
- 12:28 — Quick mitigations: reduced batch_max from 64 -> 48 for affected pool, increased CPU governor headroom on pool-2, temporarily disabled non-critical background shard compaction.
- 12:40 — Error rate dropped but p95 still elevated; opened INF-2345 to track follow-up and postmortem.
- 13:05 — Rolled a canary deploy of runbook change (draft) that throttles prefix-cache invalidations to <1/min per tenant.
- 13:30 — Observed improvement; set metric gate to leave throttling in place for 24h while we validate.

Runbook notes (drafted during shift):
- Problem statement: large concurrent prefix invalidations lead to cascading cache rebuilds and elevated KV latency; rebuilds thrash pool worker threads and trigger GC pause on Python runtimes when memory pressure spikes.
- Immediate mitigation steps (playbook):
  1) Identify offending tenant via kv-invalidations metric (query: metrics.kv.invalidations.last_10m by tenant).
  2) If invalidations > 10/min for tenant AND p95 latency > 1s, apply temporary invalidation-throttle: curl -X POST $ADMIN/api/v1/cache/throttle -d '{"tenant_id": "<TENANT>", "rate": 1}'
  3) Increase autoscaler target for affected pool (if autoscale enabled): set desired_count = desired_count + 2 (monitor for CPU > 85%).
  4) Disable shard compaction: kubectl -n runtime patch deployment shard-compactor --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'
  5) If memory pressure persists, trigger safe restart of pool nodes with staggered 30s delay.
- Notes: the POST throttle endpoint is gated and will be moved behind RBAC for Private deployments. For hosted API, SRE can run the command; for Dedicated, contact platform-eng for permission.

Changes to make to runbook (actionable):
- Add explicit metric queries (examples above) and sample commands (include kubectl context names).
- Document safe thresholds: invalidations > 10/min AND p95 > 1s as gate.
- Add a short script to apply throttles atomically across multi-region pools (TODO: Jackson + Maria).
- Add a rollback checklist for throttle mistakes (how to purge token-level throttle and re-enable compaction).

Action items and follow-ups (owners + ETA):
- INF-2345 (Priya) — Post-incident writeup due 2027-06-25. Include timeline + graphs + TTL analysis.
- INF-2362 (Maria) — Instrument cache invalidation paths to tag origin tenant lines; ETA 2027-07-02.
- Runbook script (Jackson, Maria) — Implement atomic throttle script and unit tests; ETA 2027-06-30.
- Observability (Darren) — Add a derived metric for concurrent invalidation count and dashboard tile; ETA 2027-06-28.
- Platform (oncall rotation) — Investigate upgrade path to lighter GC interpreter or offload heavy rebuilds to background worker; owner TBD.

Open questions / notes to next shift:
- Has the throttle introduced any quality regressions for multi-tenant workloads? We saw one customer report of slightly stale embeddings during 12:55-13:20 window — ticket TKT-998 attached to INF-2345.
- Are there any Dedicated customers running bespoke compaction schedules? If so, need to coordinate before enabling global throttle.
- Need confirmation from model-runtime team on memory profiling artifacts (Maria to drop links in the ticket).

Operational checklist for incoming shift (quick bullets):
- Check INF-2345 and any comments.
- Verify throttle is still active via admin endpoint and note the global rate: curl $ADMIN/api/v1/cache/throttle/status
- Watch p95 metric on /v1/generate (512+) for 30m; if p95 creeps above 1.2s, escalate to platform-eng and consider incremental rollback of batch_max change.
- Validate autoscaler steady state: ensure pool-2 CPU < 80% for 30m before scaling down.

Run commands & references captured during debugging (copy-paste friendly):
- metrics query: curl -s "https://metrics/api/v1/query?query=kv_invalidations%7Bjob%3D~\"runtime.*\"%7D%5B10m%5D" | jq '.'
- throttle apply (hosted): curl -X POST "https://admin/api/v1/cache/throttle" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant_id":"<TENANT>","rate":1}'
- disable compactor: kubectl -n runtime scale deployment/shard-compactor --replicas=0 --context=prod-east-1
- pool restart (staggered): for i in $(kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=pool-2 -o name); do kubectl delete $i --grace-period=30; sleep 30; done

Metrics snapshot at 13:45 (post-mitigation):
- /v1/generate (512+): p50 280ms, p95 930ms (down from 2.1s), error rate 0.42% (baseline 0.3%).
- KV latency p95: 120ms -> 180ms during rebuild spikes.

Escalations performed:
- Contacted platform-eng at 12:25 (paged via Ops Pager, responded 12:31, OOO follow-up requested by 14:00).
- Notified customer-success for affected tenants at 13:10; CS opened TKT-998 for end-user impact.

Misc notes / things I wrote down while triaging:
- We should consider a configurable per-tenant invalidation budget in the long-term (product idea + safety).
- Consider adding a small jitter to compaction schedules to avoid periodic alignment across our fleet.
- Reminder: add unit test in infra that simulates invalidation storms during CI for early detection.
- Next handoff: Maria (16:00-00:00 PT). If still degraded, handoff will include live run through of throttle script.

Raw attachments to include in post-incident:
- graphs: /artifacts/metrics/INF-2345/p95-latency-2027-06-22.png
- heap dumps: s3://redwood-artifacts/INF-2345/heapdump-pool-3-12-22-13-00.hprof
- profiler logs: s3://redwood-artifacts/INF-2345/profiler-13-05.tar.gz

Quick retrospective thoughts (bullet):
- Good: quick detection + throttling brought p95 down without full pool restarts.
- Needs improvement: runbook lacked the throttle endpoint example and explicit metric gates; made oncall scramble for exact thresholds.
- Followup: add a one-click dashboard action to apply throttles (product + SRE project).

If you pick this up: read INF-2345 first, then check the throttle status. Ping me on slack @priya if anything odd.

-- Priya
